payload.goal: A session should serve the initiative it is actually working on, and should be able to tell when it is not. The mechanism already exists and is correct — resolveSessionFirst treats the branch as a candidate and lets the session's home win, homeInitiative resolves by the latest session_started across every log, and every surface (statusline, SessionStart digest, hooks) follows it. What is missing is that nothing TELLS an agent to use it, and nothing tells a fresh session that the user's recent work was somewhere other than this branch. Both gaps were found by the user on 2026-08-13 after a session spent its entire life mis-homed: routing individual writes correctly with explicit initiative args while every write-back landed in the wrong record, because sofar_end_session is the one write tool that cannot be targeted.

tasks.title: The protocol block ships the trap to EVERY sofar user. It says only "Do still call `sofar_start_session`, passing the `session_id` from the injected context line" and never mentions passing `initiative` when the work moves to another record — so an agent adopts the branch's initiative and stays mis-homed for its whole life. Add the re-homing instruction with the rule of thumb that makes it stick: an `initiative` arg routes ONE write, re-homing moves the SESSION. Both dialects (CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md), since the CLI dialect has the same trap via `sofar event append`.

Protocol-block edits are VERSIONED — doctor compares the installed block against SHIPPED_PROTOCOL_BLOCKS and reports a stale one (speed-2 T6), because `sofar upgrade` replaces the binary and not repo wiring. So 1.1 means appending a new shipped version, never editing the current one in place. Verify an already-inited repo is told its block is stale rather than silently keeping the old text.

DECIDE whether sofar_end_session should take an `initiative` at all. It is the ONLY write tool that cannot be targeted, which is what turns a mis-homed session into ~10 misrouted write-backs. But adding it would legitimise the session SPLIT that record-integrity spent a whole initiative eliminating (D13, and the 21 splits accepted as history). Weigh teaching re-homing (1.1) as the complete fix against widening the tool surface; cite record-integrity D13 either way.

DECIDE what a brand-new session on a BOUND branch is told. Today it silently gets the branch's initiative, which in a repo like this one is wrong most of the time — main is bound to drift-certification while five initiatives are live. The user's ask is that a new session load the LAST worked initiative. The tension to resolve honestly: 'last worked' is global, so it can be a PEER's work, and silently loading it recreates exactly the misrouting class record-integrity fixed. Weigh (a) resolve to most-recently-active, (b) keep branch resolution but ADD a visible line naming the more recent work and how to re-home, (c) track last-worked per machine. Option (b) is the one consistent with the standing rule that a wrong answer is worse than a missing one.

Implement 2.1's choice inside the ≤10,000-char SessionStart guarantee, and WITHOUT adding an unconditional line — it must stay quiet when the branch and the recent work agree, which is the common case in a single-initiative repo. A nudge that fires every session is one people learn to skip (record-integrity D3).

Cost check before it ships: 'most recently active initiative' means reading N logs, and the SessionStart budget is 100ms with roughly 65ms already spent. core/warmth.ts already answers recency from a log's own newest event rather than filesystem mtime — reuse it rather than adding a scan, and measure before and after like D6 did.

Dogfood the exact case that prompted this: from a session on a branch bound elsewhere, confirm the fresh-session surface names the right record, that re-homing moves the statusline and the write-back target together, and that peer sessions on the old initiative are UNAFFECTED — the property that makes per-session pinning safe. Verified once already by hand on 2026-08-13; make it a test.
docs/SPEC.md: the re-homing contract and the fresh-session resolution order, alongside the session-before-branch precedence initiative-lifecycle already recorded there.

payload.text:
Opened 2026-08-13, split out of commit-attribution because that initiative is about binding commits and reviewing execution, while this is about how a session picks its record. Created with --no-bind: main carries drift-certification and several initiatives are live in one worktree, so binding would knock a peer's record off the branch it resolves through.

NOTHING IS BROKEN in the mechanism, and that is the point of this record. Verified by hand on 2026-08-13: one sofar_start_session call carrying an explicit `initiative` moved a live session's statusline from "drift-certification 15/25" to "commit-attribution 15/24", left bindings.json untouched, and left three peer drift-certification sessions unaffected. resolveSessionFirst, homeInitiative, the statusline and the hooks are all correct. Do not rebuild any of it.

What is missing is entirely on the TELLING side, and both gaps cost real work before being noticed:
- the shipped protocol block never mentions re-homing, so an agent adopts the branch's initiative and stays mis-homed for its whole life (Phase 1)
- a fresh session on a bound branch is told nothing about more recent work elsewhere (Phase 2)

The evidence is a session that spent its entire life mis-homed: it routed every decision, task update and note correctly by passing `initiative` explicitly, and still filed roughly ten write-backs in the wrong record, because sofar_end_session is the only write tool that cannot be targeted. Its own history is in commit-attribution's log and the repo-memory entries there.

NEXT: task 1.1, the protocol-block instruction — it is the cheapest fix and it removes a trap every sofar user currently inherits.

payload.text:
Measured 2026-08-13, and it constrains 2.1 before it is designed.

THE RECORD CANNOT SAY WHICH SESSION OPENED AN INITIATIVE. All 38 initiative_created events in this repo carry session `cli` — the sentinel `sofar new` stamps when no session id is passed, since it is a CLI command with no MCP pin. So "the last initiative I opened" is not answerable from the log today, and 2.1 must not assume it is. Either it settles for "most recently ACTIVE" (which core/warmth.ts already answers from each log's newest event), or `sofar new` starts attributing creation to the calling session — a small change, but it is a change, and it only helps from the day it lands since history is never rewritten.

SPLITS ARE COMMON, NOT EXCEPTIONAL: 28 of 160 sessions are registered in more than one record — 17.5%, about one session in six. That is the empirical case for Phase 1: this is not a rare mishap worth a footnote, it is the normal outcome of an agent adopting a branch's initiative and then working somewhere else. Note the figure is a CEILING on the problem, not a measure of harm — record-integrity graded splits by liveness and deliberately accepted ended ones as settled history, so some of the 28 are benign.

Add as task 2.4 when the plan is next rewritten: decide whether `sofar new` should stamp the calling session, weighing that it makes creation attributable against the fact that it helps no existing record.

payload.note: Mechanism re-verified in source before writing a word of instruction: sofar_start_session re-homes on an explicit `initiative` (start-session.ts:24-36 — the arg beats homeInitiative, and an unregistered session gets a session_started appended into the new log, which is what moves every downstream surface through resolveSessionFirst). sofar_end_session takes no initiative (end-session.ts:67 folds homeInitiative). The CLI dialect's trap is DIFFERENT and worse than assumed: `sofar event append [slug]` does take a positional slug (event.ts:1467, runAppend:1377 `ctx.resolveInitiative(args.slug)`), but never consults homeInitiative — so the CLI has no session home at all and the slug must be repeated on EVERY append. The shipped AGENTS.md block never mentions the positional.

payload.because:
The capability already exists; only the instruction was missing. endSession routes the ACTIVE session's write-back through the context pin (mcp/end-session.ts:100), and startSession sets that pin to an explicitly named initiative (mcp/start-session.ts:24-36, 56, 69) — so ONE re-home call moves the write-back target, and record-integrity D8 already routes a non-active session home then branch. Verified by hand 2026-08-13: a re-home moved the statusline and left three peer sessions untouched.

An `initiative` arg would do something the record has no semantics for: append a session_ended into a log holding no session_started for that id — a session that ends where it never began. That is precisely the split shape record-integrity D1 and D2 exist to eliminate and D3 accepted 21 of as unrepairable history, in its worst variant: the record holding the work carries no wrap-up, and the record holding the wrap-up carries no work. Every read surface keys on registration (sessions/<id>.md, overlappingWritebacks, homeInitiative's latest-wins under D9).

It would also leave the Stop gate armed. The gate resolves through the session's home (resolveSessionFirst), so a write-back deliberately filed elsewhere blocks the session on debt in a log its own write-back can never reach — the exact failure D9 names, reintroduced through a new door.

And re-homing is strictly better than per-call targeting on the merits: it moves EVERY surface together — statusline, the SessionStart digest on resume, hook events, the Stop gate — where an arg fixes one event and leaves the rest torn. The rule of thumb now in the protocol block ("an initiative arg routes ONE write, re-homing moves the SESSION") is that difference stated in the one place an agent reads it.

Citation correction: task 1.3's text cites record-integrity D13, which does not exist — that initiative logged D1 through D9. The load-bearing ones are D1, D2, D3, D8, D9.

Residual gap, closed in the other dialect rather than here: the CLI path has no re-homing AT ALL, because `sofar event append` resolves its slug through ctx.resolveInitiative (cli/event.ts:1377) and never consults homeInitiative. So AGENTS.md's new RECORD clause tells those tools to pass the leading slug on every append, the session_ended one above all.
payload.chose: sofar_end_session keeps its three-argument signature: no `initiative` arg, ever. The write-back stays untargetable BY DESIGN, and teaching re-homing (task 1.1) is the complete fix rather than a partial one.
payload.over: Adding an optional `initiative` to sofar_end_session — a SPEC §MCP tools signature change — so a mis-homed session could redirect its write-back per call without moving itself.
payload.rule: Never give sofar_end_session an `initiative` argument — a write-back belongs where the session lives; move the SESSION with sofar_start_session instead.

payload.note: Both dialects now name the record a write lands in. CLAUDE.md gains a RE-HOME bullet carrying the rule of thumb (an `initiative` arg routes ONE write, re-homing moves the SESSION) and the reason it is the fix rather than a nicety — sofar_end_session takes no initiative and always follows the home. AGENTS.md gains a RECORD bullet, and the CLI trap turned out to be sharper than the task assumed: `sofar event append` DOES take a leading slug positional, but resolves it through the branch and never homeInitiative, so there is no session home on that path at all. Every append shown in the loop now carries `<slug>`, session_ended included, and `sofar remember` is named with its `--initiative` form since it is a flag there, not a positional.

Versioned, not edited in place: the shipping CLAUDE.md block became PROTOCOL_BLOCK_V4 and the AGENTS.md one AGENTS_PROTOCOL_BLOCK_V3, both appended to their ledgers, and both proved byte-exact against git HEAD by extracting the template literals and comparing (the five older entries proved unchanged the same way). Four tests pin the result: the two content assertions, a ledger-wide check that EVERY shipped block in BOTH dialects classifies as `stale` against its current template, an init run refreshing a repo sitting on the immediately-previous pair, and a doctor run reporting that repo as "from an older sofar" rather than customized — doctor is the half that matters for a repo which never re-runs init, since `sofar upgrade` replaces the binary and not repo wiring.
Decided against the arg; reasoning in the decision logged this session. Phase 1 is complete.

payload.because:
(a) is not a display change, which is what settles it. resolveBound feeds handlePostTool and every other hook (cli/event.ts:445, 519), so "most recently active" would redirect where hook events LAND, not merely what the agent reads. Implemented display-only it is worse: a digest describing a record the session is not writing to is the torn-session shape record-integrity D9 names. And "last worked" is GLOBAL — in this worktree alone five initiatives are live under peer sessions, so the newest append is routinely a peer's, and silently adopting it recreates the misrouting class D1 and D2 closed.

(c) buys nothing against that. The concurrency that makes "last worked" ambiguous here is not across machines, it is inside ONE worktree, and per-machine state cannot separate two peer sessions sharing a checkout. It also reintroduces exactly the side index record-integrity D1 rejected: duplicated state that can desync from the log it summarises, needs pruning, and forces a SPEC record-layout change plus a gitignore ruling.

(b) keeps the property that makes the whole mechanism safe: the record answers what it knows, and where it cannot know, it names the candidate rather than guessing. What has changed since that was merely a nice idea is that task 1.1 shipped re-homing in the protocol block, so an agent reading the line now has the vocabulary and the one call to act on it. Naming without a remedy would have been noise.

Gate 1 is `via === 'branch'` because a session whose own home answered has already CHOSEN, and telling it about newer work elsewhere is second-guessing a deliberate act. For a brand-new session, lazy registration (record-integrity D2) means no home exists yet, so via is always 'branch' — the gate reads as "fresh, or settled on the branch's record", both of which are cases where the branch is the only thing that spoke.

Gate 2 keeps it silent whenever the bound record IS the most recent — every session in a single-initiative repo, which is most users. A line that fires every session is one people learn to skip, the failure record-integrity D3 named about a permanently red doctor.

Deliberately stateless: no "already told you" marker, following record-integrity D5 — repeating a true fact costs less than storing one, and a marker is the same side store (c) was rejected for.

Three honesty requirements on the wording, since a line that overclaims is worse than none: state BOTH last-touched ages so the reader can judge the gap; never assert the newer work is the user's, because it may be a peer's; and make re-homing conditional on it being the work they were asked to continue. The line is also distinct from the existing "Adjacent records" line and must not read as a variant of it — adjacency is shared FILES, this is recency, and neither is a rule.
payload.chose: Option (b), with two gates. A fresh session on a bound branch keeps BRANCH resolution exactly as it is, and the SessionStart digest gains ONE conditional preface line naming the more recently written record and how to re-home into it. Gate 1: resolution came from the branch rather than the session's own home (resolveSessionFirst's `via`). Gate 2: some other initiative's log carries a strictly newer last append than the bound one's. No side store, no change to routing, no unconditional line.
payload.over: (a) resolving a fresh session to the most-recently-active initiative, and (c) tracking last-worked per machine in a side store.
payload.rule: A fresh session's record is resolved by the branch — never silently redirect resolution to the most recently active initiative. Name the candidate and let the session re-home.

payload.note: Decided (b), reasoning in the decision logged this session. The fact that settled it was not in the task text: resolveBound feeds handlePostTool and every other hook, so option (a) would have moved where hook events LAND rather than only what the agent reads. Option (c) collapsed on inspection too — the ambiguity here is peer sessions inside ONE worktree, which per-machine state cannot separate.

payload.note: recentWorkElsewhereNotice in cli/event.ts, added as the FIRST preface part in handleSessionStart — it leads because every other part of that output describes the bound record, and this line questions whether the bound record is the right one at all. resolveBound now carries resolveSessionFirst's `via` (it was discarding it), which is gate 1; gate 2 is a strictly newer last append in some other log. A third suppression fell out of building it and was not in the plan: a record whose newest event is initiative_status_changed was just closed or reopened rather than worked, so it is skipped — offering a just-closed record to a fresh session is exactly the wrong answer this line exists to avoid, and real work appending past the status change brings it back. Eight tests in test/recent-elsewhere.test.ts, most of them about SILENCE: single-initiative repo, bound record already newest, session that has its own home, just-closed record, unreadable bound log.

Measured on this repo's real record — 38 initiatives, 5.3 MB of logs. The scan costs 1.69 to 1.74 ms, which is one tail read per initiative at 0.032 ms each; warmth's newestEvent is O(1) in log size, so a 9 MB log answers as fast as a 5 KB one and the cost tracks initiative COUNT, never accumulated history. Gated out by via=session it is 0.0000 ms, returning before any read at all. End to end on a copy of the real record: SessionStart 23.7 ms with the line against 22.0 ms without, a 7.4 percent share, in-process and excluding node boot. Two findings on 2.2's `recentWorkElsewhereNotice`, from a code-review pass run by commit-attribution over 0415062..HEAD. That range caught this code UNCOMMITTED in the shared worktree, so it was reviewed as in-flight work rather than as a landed change — treat it as an early read, not a verdict, and re-check both against whatever finally lands.

1. CLOSED RECORDS STAY ELIGIBLE. The suppression only fires when `initiative_status_changed` is the single NEWEST event, so any later append re-qualifies a finished initiative. Measured on this repo: of 8 closed initiatives, 6 have events after their close event — drift-hardening 27, record-index 20, scanner-version-gate 7, record-citations 3, session-orientation 3, engine-audit 1. A fresh branch-bound session is then told "More recent work is in ANOTHER record: drift-hardening … re-home now", pointing at a record that is done and unbound. The fold already holds `state.status`; the one-event peek is a proxy for it that any hook-appended file_touched or command_run, or a post-close session_ended, defeats. recent-elsewhere.test.ts:145 currently PINS the proxy behaviour as desired, so the test would need inverting with it.

2. NO RECENCY FLOOR AND NO MARGIN. The line fires on any strictly-newer sibling log. In a repo like this one — 20+ initiatives, concurrent sessions appending constantly — the bound record is almost never the newest log, so the notice renders on essentially every branch-resolved SessionStart. That is the "a line that fires every session is one people learn to skip" failure its own docblock cites record-integrity D3 against; the gates it relies on hold for single-initiative repos. Separately there is no absolute floor: a dormant repo whose bound record last moved 400d ago and whose sibling moved 335d ago still renders "re-home now", which is advice with no basis. A minimum recency, and/or a minimum GAP between the two timestamps, is what is missing.
